items.title: TDAC arrival card: required
items.text: Every foreign visitor must fill in the free Thailand Digital Arrival Card online before arrival. You can send it in the 3 days (72 hours) before you land. For 8 Jan, do it on 6 or 7 Jan; the arrival day also works. Have your flight number and hotel address ready. Save the confirmation on your phone.

links.label: Royal Thai Embassy: how to submit the TDAC

items.title: Fake TDAC websites
items.text: Use only tdac.immigration.go.th. Fake sites look official, charge about 20-90 USD and steal passport data. In March 2026 Immigration said about 1 in 10 foreign arrivals had used a fake site. The real TDAC is always free. Immigration's new THIM app is optional. Report fakes to the Cyber Police on 1441.

items.title: Visa-free stay is now 30 days
items.text: Since 15 Sep 2026 the visa-free stay is 30 days (not 60), for tourism only. It covers 60 countries, including all EU states, the UK, US, Israel, Georgia and Ukraine. Russia and Kazakhstan also get 30 days under bilateral deals. Your 8-26 Jan trip (19 days) fits. Check your passport on the Thai e-Visa site.

items.title: Passport, ticket and money
items.text: Your passport must be valid at least 6 months after arrival and have a free page. Officers may ask for a ticket out of Thailand within 30 days, your hotel booking and proof of money (10,000-20,000 baht per person; sources differ). Checks are random, but some people were refused entry. Keep these papers on your phone.

links.label: Royal Thai Embassy London: visa exemption

items.title: Customs: cigarette limit
items.text: You may bring at most 200 cigarettes (1 carton) per person. Customs checks this on arrival. Above the limit, the cigarettes are usually taken and the fine can be 10 times their value. Vapes and heated-tobacco devices are banned completely (see Safety and law).

items.title: No ETA needed
items.text: The planned Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) has not started (Oct 2026). In 2025 Thailand replaced the plan with the TDAC. If your passport is visa-exempt, the TDAC is the only online form you need before the trip.

items.title: Tourist entry fee: not yet
items.text: A 450-baht entry fee for foreign visitors is planned. The target is early 2027, first for air arrivals. In Oct 2026 it still needed Cabinet approval and a Royal Gazette notice, so it is not in force yet, and the plan can still change. Check the news before you fly.

items.title: Flights via the Middle East
items.text: The UK government warns that the conflict in the Middle East has closed some airspace and caused delays and cancellations (Oct 2026). If your flight goes via the Gulf, check it with your airline before you leave. Make sure your travel insurance covers flight disruption.

items.title: Grab and Bolt
items.text: Both apps work in Phuket and show the price first. Typical car fares: airport to Patong 600-950 baht, Patong to Kata 250-500, Patong to Old Town 400-550. Bolt is often a bit cheaper, so compare. Prices go up at busy times and in heavy rain. If pickup is hard, walk to the main road.

items.title: From the airport
items.text: Grab pickup is near Exit 8 (international) or Exit 1 (domestic). Airport limousine taxis have fixed prices on a board, about 800 baht to Patong; metered taxis add a 100-baht airport fee. Cheapest: Smart Bus (100 baht) to the west-coast beaches, or the Airport Bus (100 baht) to Phuket Town.

items.title: Taxis and tuk-tuks: agree the price first
items.text: Street taxis and tuk-tuks almost never use the meter. They quote fixed prices, often much higher than the apps (Patong to Kata about 500-600 baht; Grab about 250-350). Agree the price before you get in and show the app price to bargain. Carry small notes. If a driver cheats you, call the Tourist Police on 1155.

items.title: Scooter rental: licence and insurance
items.text: To ride legally you need a motorcycle licence from home plus an International Driving Permit that covers motorcycles. Without them, insurance usually pays nothing after a crash. Many rental scooters are not registered, so check the papers. Police checks are common. Never leave your passport as a deposit.

items.title: Helmets and road safety
items.text: Rider and passenger must wear a helmet; since June 2025 the fine is up to 2,000 baht. Thailand drives on the left. Phuket roads are steep, curvy and busy. Do not ride after drinking. After a party, Grab or a taxi is the safer choice.

items.title: Phuket Smart Bus
items.text: Route 1: Airport - Patong - Karon - Kata - Rawai, flat 100 baht. Route 2: Bus Terminal 2 - Phuket Town - Patong, 50 baht. The Dragon Line in Old Town is free. Pay by contactless card, Thai QR or cash. Last bus from the airport 23:30; last bus from Rawai to the airport 19:30.

links.label: Smart Bus timetable and live tracking

items.title: Local songthaew buses
items.text: Open-sided songthaew buses leave Ranong Road (near the market) in Phuket Town for the main beaches, about every 30 minutes from about 06:00 to 18:00. They cost about 30-50 baht but are slow and do not run in the evening.

items.title: Typical drive times
items.text: From the airport: Patong 50-90 min, Kata 60-90 min, Old Town 40-60 min, Natai (Phang Nga) 30-45 min. Patong to Kata 20-30 min, Patong to Old Town 30-45 min. Traffic is worst in the late afternoon, so leave early for flights.

items.title: Koh Phangan: fastest (fly + boat)
items.text: There is no direct boat. Fly Phuket - Koh Samui with Bangkok Airways (55 min, 6-7 flights a day, about 3,000-5,000 baht one way in late 2026). From Samui airport, a Lomprayah van + boat goes to Koh Phangan: about 500 baht, or 700 to your hotel, 1-2 hours. Door to door about 5 hours.

items.title: Koh Phangan: one bus + boat ticket
items.text: Lomprayah sells one ticket: bus to Donsak pier, then a fast boat. Pickup about 07:30 at hotels in Patong, Kata, Karon, Rawai and Nai Harn, or 10:00 at Phuket airport. You reach Koh Phangan about 16:30. About 1,600 baht, or 1,800 with hotel drop-off (2026 timetable). Book a few days ahead.

items.title: Koh Phangan: cheapest and slowest
items.text: Public bus from Phuket Bus Terminal 2 to Surat Thani (about 4 hours), van to Donsak pier (about 1 hour), then a ferry to Thong Sala (about 2.5 hours). Total about 8-9 hours and roughly 600-900 baht. Only worth it on a tight budget.

items.title: Party trips: book early
items.text: Flights, boats and rooms on Koh Phangan sell out around big party dates. Book early and check the last boat back. Koh Phangan's rainy season is roughly October to December. January still gets some showers (about 130 mm on 8 to 9 days, against about 30 mm in Phuket), so rain and choppy seas are more likely there. Do not plan a tight connection to a flight home.

items.title: Phi Phi ferries from Rassada Pier
items.text: Big ferries leave Rassada Pier (near Phuket Town) at about 08:30, 11:00, 13:30 and 15:00. They take about 2 hours and cost about 500-700 baht. Speedboats take about 1 hour for 750-850 baht. Pay the 20-baht island fee in cash at Tonsai pier.

items.title: Maya Bay and park fee
items.text: Trips to Maya Bay and Phi Phi Le pay a national park fee: 400 baht for foreign adults, 200 for children. Some tours include it, others collect cash on the day. Swimming at Maya Bay is not allowed. The bay closes every year from 1 Aug to 30 Sep, so it is open in January.

items.title: Krabi and Ao Nang
items.text: Boats also run from Rassada Pier to Ao Nang in Krabi. The fastest speedboats take about 1-1.5 hours; ferries that stop at Phi Phi take much longer. Schedules change by season, so check times on 12Go.

items.title: Day tours: Chalong and Ao Po piers
items.text: Many speedboat day tours (Phi Phi, Racha, Coral Island) leave from Chalong Pier in the south. Some boats leave from Ao Po Grand Marina in the north-east. Most tours include hotel pickup. Ask which pier before you book.

items.title: How to book boats
items.text: Book on 12Go or on the official sites (Lomprayah, Seatran, Bangkok Airways). Save e-tickets offline. Arrive at the pier 30-45 minutes early to swap the e-ticket for a boarding pass.

items.title: Plan for the week
items.text: Go after the big group leaves: fly to Samui on Mon 18 Jan if they leave that morning, or on Tue 19. Mon 18: Chill Up and maybe a Seaside pre-Full Moon party. Tue 19: OXA or the Lighthouse. Wed 20: Waterfall. Thu 21: Jungle Experience. Fri 22: the Full Moon Party. Sat 23: boat to Samui and the 15:05 flight back to Phuket for Circoloco.

items.title: Fastest way: fly Phuket to Koh Samui, then a boat
items.text: Bangkok Airways is the only nonstop airline from Phuket (HKT) to Koh Samui (USM). On Mon 18 and Tue 19 Jan 2027 there are 8 flights a day, 55 minutes: 07:30, 09:45, 11:00, 12:55, 14:15, 16:35, 17:30 and 19:55, from about 4,730 THB one way (Google Flights, 16 Oct 2026). Take the 14:15 flight or earlier. Later flights miss the last boats to Thong Sala; only the Haad Rin Queen speedboat at 18:30 still goes to Haad Rin.

items.title: Samui airport to Koh Phangan in one ticket
items.text: Lomprayah sells airport-to-Phangan tickets with the van to Bangrak pier included: about every hour from 07:30 to 15:00 and a last one at 17:00, 500 THB, about 1 hour to Thong Sala pier (700 THB with a drop at your hotel; 2026 timetable). Seatran Discovery has airport departures at 07:30, 09:00, 12:00 and 14:00 on 18-19 Jan 2027, also 500 THB (670 THB to your hotel).

items.title: Pier to pier: Samui to Koh Phangan
items.text: From Bangrak pier (near the airport) Lomprayah boats leave about every hour from 08:00 to 17:30, 350 THB, 30 minutes to Thong Sala; Seatran leaves at 08:00, 09:30, 12:30 and 14:30 (350 THB). The Haad Rin Queen goes from Bangrak straight to Haad Rin: ferry 10:30 and 17:00 (200 THB, 50 min), speedboat 15:00 and 18:30 (500 THB, 25 min).

items.title: Bus + boat from Phuket in one ticket (slow but cheap)
items.text: Lomprayah picks you up in Patong, Kata, Karon, Rawai or Nai Harn at 07:30, or at Phuket airport (gate 1-2) at 10:00, and you reach Koh Phangan at 16:30 by bus and catamaran: 1,600 THB, or 1,800 THB with a drop at your hotel. From its Phuket Town office it leaves at 09:30 for 1,400 THB. Kamala is not in the pickup zone. Cheaper bus + ferry tickets via Surat Thani (Phantip, Raja Ferry and others) cost about 600-900 THB and take most of the day.

items.title: Raja car ferry (only with a car or a bus ticket)
items.text: Raja Ferry crosses from Donsak on the mainland to Thong Sala at 05:00, 08:00, 11:00, 14:00 and 18:00 (2 h 30 min), and from Lipa Noi on Samui in about 1 h 30 min. It is slow; you only use it on a bus + ferry ticket or with a car.

items.title: Back to Phuket on Sat 23 Jan for Circoloco
items.text: Samui to Phuket flights on Sat 23 Jan 2027: 08:15, 09:20, 11:10, 15:05, 15:50, 18:15 and 19:00 (1 hour, about 4,900 THB on 16 Oct 2026). The realistic plan after the Full Moon night: a 10:30 or 11:00 Seatran boat (or the 10:45 Lomprayah) from Thong Sala to Bangrak, then the 15:05 flight; you land at 16:05 and reach Baba Beach Club Natai (about 30 min) around 17:00. Circoloco runs 15:00-03:00. Book this flight now: there are only 7 a day.

items.title: Earliest boats from Koh Phangan on Sat 23 Jan
items.text: From Thong Sala the first boat is the Lomprayah speedboat at 07:30 to Bangrak (arrives 08:00, 350 THB; 2026 timetable). With its van ticket (500 THB) you are at Samui airport at 08:30, in time for the 09:20 flight. Later: Seatran 10:30 and 11:00 (500 THB with the airport transfer, at the airport 12:00 or 12:30). From Haad Rin: Haad Rin Queen ferry 09:30 (200 THB) or speedboat 12:30 (500 THB) to Bangrak.

items.title: Backup if the flights are full
items.text: The Lomprayah bus + boat leaves Thong Sala at 11:00 and reaches its Phuket Town office at 18:30 (1,400 THB, 2026 timetable). Other bus + ferry tickets to Phuket Bus Terminal 2 leave in the morning and take 10-12 hours; check 12Go for times. From Phuket Town it is about 1 hour by taxi north to Natai.

items.title: Full Moon week: rooms cost more, book now
items.text: In party week rooms near Haad Rin cost about 2-3 times the normal price, and many places ask for a 3-5 night minimum stay. Haad Rin sells out weeks before, and January is also peak season. Book in October or November. Ban Tai and Thong Sala are much cheaper bases.

items.title: Where to stay: Ban Tai is the best base
items.text: Most parties this week are in the Ban Tai hills or on its beach: OXA, Jungle Experience, Waterfall, Retro Mountain, Unclave, Chill Up and Sabaii. Haad Rin (Full Moon, Lighthouse, taxi boats to Eden) is 10-20 minutes away by taxi, and Thong Sala pier about 10 minutes. Stay in Haad Rin only if you want to walk home from the Full Moon Party and accept the minimum stay.

items.title: Getting around at night
items.text: Shared taxis (pickup trucks, called songthaew) run late between Thong Sala, Ban Tai and Haad Rin on party nights. They have no meter, so agree the price per person before you get in. A guide gives about 200 THB per person from Thong Sala to Haad Rin. For Eden Garden and Bambu take a 4x4 truck from the Ban Tai 7-Eleven or a taxi boat from Haad Rin.

items.title: Scooters: better not at night
items.text: Thai law requires a helmet. Many rental scooters are not registered for the road, and without a licence that covers motorbikes your travel insurance may not pay (UK travel advice). A scooter rental blog says the steep Haad Rin hill and riding home after drinking are the two biggest causes of scooter accidents on Koh Phangan. On party nights take a taxi.

links.label: Scooter to the Full Moon Party (Byklo, 2026)

items.title: Full Moon Party safety
items.text: Buy your own bucket and watch it being mixed: drinks are strong, spiking happens, and drinks with methanol can kill (UK travel advice). Stay away from the fire rope and fire limbo, and do not swim at night. Leave passport and cards in the room safe, carry a photo of your passport and small cash, and agree a meeting point with your friend.

items.title: Drugs, vapes and police
items.text: Even small amounts of drugs can mean heavy fines or prison, and police are active on party nights. Vapes and e-cigarettes are illegal in Thailand: fines are usually 5,000-30,000 THB, with no exception for tourists. In an emergency call the Tourist Police on 1155.

items.title: What to bring
items.text: Cash: the Full Moon entry (200 THB), the taxis, and OXA and the Hollystone bar take cash only. ATMs in Haad Rin can run out around the full moon, and each withdrawal costs 250-350 THB. Bring closed shoes (broken glass on the sand), clothes you do not mind ruining with UV paint, a waterproof phone pouch, a small torch for the paths to Eden and Lighthouse, a power bank, and your passport or ID (Jungle Experience and Hollystone are 20+).

items.title: Find each week's parties
items.text: Most January line-ups and small parties are posted only 1-2 weeks before. Check the phangan.events calendar and the Phangan Party Guide channel on Telegram, which posts the parties of each day.

items.title: If you stay longer on Koh Phangan
items.text: If you skip Circoloco: Eden Garden and Hollystone (Sat 23), Waterfall, Bambu and a WET pool party (Sun 24). Fly back to Phuket on Mon 25 Jan (Samui flights from 08:15 to 19:00). Do not leave it for Tue 26: a late boat or a delayed Samui flight could make you miss the 18:20 flight home.

items.title: Tourist SIM or eSIM
items.text: AIS and True sell tourist plans with unlimited 5G/4G data. AIS 2026 prices: 8 days 499 baht, 15 days 699 baht. True: 15 days 699, 30 days 1,199. For 8-26 Jan (19 days) take a 30-day plan (True: 1,199 baht) or a 15-day plan plus a top-up. You need your passport to register.

items.title: Airport counter or eSIM before you fly
items.text: AIS and True counters are in the international arrivals hall at Phuket airport. Or buy an AIS or True eSIM online before the trip, or use an eSIM app such as Airalo. Check that your phone supports eSIM. Keep your home SIM on for bank SMS codes.

items.title: Wi-Fi
items.text: Most hotels, cafes and malls have free Wi-Fi. AIS tourist plans include AIS Super WiFi hotspots. Signal can be weak on boats and small islands, so download maps and tickets before you go.

items.title: Vapes and e-cigarettes are illegal
items.text: It is illegal to bring, own or use any vape, e-cigarette, pod, e-liquid or heated-tobacco device (like IQOS). There are no exceptions for tourists. Penalties: confiscation, fines of about 5,000-30,000 baht, detention and court. You may have to stay in Thailand until the case ends. Leave it at home.

items.title: Drugs: very strict laws
items.text: Even small amounts of drugs can mean heavy fines, prison, deportation and a ban from Thailand. Police raid parties and villas, also on Koh Phangan, and do urine tests; a positive test can lead to charges. Serious cases can mean life in prison or the death penalty. Never carry anything for others.

items.title: New deportation rules
items.text: Since 28 Aug 2026 Thailand can deport foreigners without a criminal conviction if officials decide their behaviour is against public order or public morals. People who are deported may not be allowed back. Follow local laws and police instructions.

links.label: UK travel advice: safety and law

items.title: Cannabis: medical use only
items.text: Since June 2025 cannabis is for medical use only: you need a Thai prescription (max 30-day supply). Recreational use is illegal, even though you still see shops. Do not smoke in public. Taking cannabis out of Thailand is a crime: fines from 30,000 baht per kg and an immigration watchlist.

items.title: Drink spiking and fake alcohol
items.text: At parties, never leave your drink alone and do not accept open drinks from strangers. Methanol in fake or cheap spirits can kill; get help fast if someone has blurred vision or feels very sick after drinking. Plan your ride home before you go out.

items.title: Alcohol sale hours
items.text: Shops and most bars may sell alcohol from 11:00 to midnight; the old 14:00-17:00 ban has ended. Licensed hotels, clubs and airports may serve outside these hours. The legal drinking age is 20. Since Nov 2025, drinkers can also be fined up to 10,000 baht for drinking at banned times or places.

items.title: No smoking on the beach
items.text: Since 2018 smoking is banned on Patong Beach and other listed Thai beaches: fine up to 100,000 baht and/or up to 1 year in jail. Use the marked smoking areas and never leave cigarette butts. Smoking in other public places can also bring a fine of up to 5,000 baht.

links.label: The Nation: Patong beach smoking ban

items.title: Jet-ski scams
items.text: Some jet-ski operators blame tourists for old damage and ask for big money. Never leave your passport as a deposit. Film the jet ski from all sides before you ride. If there is a dispute, stay calm and call the Tourist Police on 1155.

items.title: Rip currents and flags
items.text: In January the west-coast sea is usually calm, but rip currents still happen. Swim near lifeguards and never swim at a red flag. If a current pulls you out, do not fight it: swim parallel to the beach, then back in. Do not swim drunk or at night.

items.title: Drones need permits
items.text: Register every drone with the NBTC within 30 days of arrival; camera drones also need CAAT registration (with a Thai SIM). You need 1 million baht third-party insurance and CAAT approval at least 3 days before each flight. No flying within 9 km of airports. Unregistered drone: up to 100,000 baht and/or 5 years in jail.

items.title: Carry ID
items.text: Police can ask to see your passport. Carry it, or at least a copy of the photo page and entry stamp. A copy is usually fine, but you may have to show the original at a police station within 24 hours.

items.title: Social hostels in Patong
items.text: Mad Monkey Phuket (Patong, 9.8 on Hostelworld) has a 'Meet Up' every evening at 19:00 with half-price beer, pub crawls on Tuesday and Thursday and a foam party on Saturday. Lub d Patong has pool party nights; Zostel Patong has daily pub crawls and pool parties. Dorm beds at Mad Monkey and Lub d: about 1,000-1,400 baht a night on 23-25 Jan.

items.title: Hostelworld app chats
items.text: Book a bed through Hostelworld, and the app opens chats with people in your hostel and in Phuket 7 days before check-in. 'Linkups' are meet-ups that hostels and travellers post, from dinners to nights out.

items.title: Find the techno people
items.text: Check Resident Advisor with the location set to Thailand (its Phuket page stays empty; Shelter has a club page there), and the Instagram pages of Shelter, Courage Bar and SUB (FAKE PALM nights show up on RA and Megatix): small parties are posted only 1-3 weeks ahead. Go early, stand near the booth and talk to the DJs and bar staff. They know the after-parties.

items.title: Join-in boat trips
items.text: Group boat tours are sold per person, so going alone costs the same. Examples: Khai Islands half day about 1,100 baht, James Bond Island 1,400-3,500, Phi Phi by speedboat 1,500-3,500. Pickup is often extra from Kamala or Nai Yang, and ask if the park fee is included. Book 1-2 days ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide.

items.title: Drinks at parties
items.text: Buy your own drinks and watch them being poured, or take closed cans and bottles. Never leave a drink alone, and never take pills or open drinks from strangers. Police raid parties and do urine tests, and drug use is a crime. If you suddenly feel very drunk or sick, tell security and call 1669.

links.label: UK travel advice: safety and law
Party raid with urine tests (Khaosod, Oct 2025)

items.title: Plan the ride home
items.text: Before you go out, check that Grab or Bolt works from the venue and keep at least 1,000 baht in cash for the ride, more for long rides. For Circoloco in Natai (Sat 23 Jan, until 03:00), book a driver for both ways. In Grab, use 'Share My Ride' so a friend can follow your car live.

items.title: Phone, money and passport
items.text: Clubs check your age (20+) with your passport, so carry it in a zip pocket and leave spare cards and most cash in the hotel safe. Take one card and some cash. Charge your phone, bring a small power bank and save your hotel in Google Maps offline.

items.title: Share your location
items.text: Before a night out, share your live location with a friend: Google Maps can share until you turn it off, and WhatsApp for up to 8 hours. Send the party name, your hotel and when you plan to be back. Message 'home safe' when you arrive.

items.title: Help numbers
items.text: Tourist Police 1155 (English, 24 hours), ambulance 1669, police 191. The Thailand Tourist Police app has an SOS button that sends your GPS position, and a live chat with officers in English. Install it before you go out.

items.title: Budget for a room alone
items.text: Most hotel rooms cost the same for one person as for two. For 23-26 Jan, expect about 400-1,800 baht for a dorm bed, 800-1,400 for a private room with a shared bathroom, and 2,100-3,600 for a room with your own bathroom or a mid-range hotel. Saturday 23 Jan is often the most expensive night.

items.title: Bangkok Hospital Phuket (private)
items.text: Large private hospital in Phuket Town (2/1 Hongyok Utis Road) with English-speaking staff and a 24-hour emergency room. Emergency: 1719 from a Thai number, or +66 76 254 425. It is expensive, so have travel insurance.

items.title: Bangkok Hospital Siriroj (private)
items.text: Big private hospital of the same group, on the bypass road near Central Phuket (44 Chalermprakiat Ror 9 Road). English-speaking staff and a 24-hour emergency room. Phone +66 76 361 888; emergency 1719 from a Thai number.

items.title: Mission Hospital Phuket (private)
items.text: Mid-size private hospital at 4/1 Thepkrasattri Road in Phuket Town, with a 24-hour emergency room. Usually cheaper than the Bangkok Hospital group. Phone +66 76 237 220.

items.title: Vachira Phuket Hospital (government)
items.text: Phuket's main government hospital (353 Yaowarat Road, Phuket Town) with a 24-hour emergency and trauma centre. Cheaper, but waits can be long and English can be limited. Phone +66 76 361 234.

items.title: Patong Hospital (government)
items.text: Small government hospital in Patong (57 Sai Nam Yen Road), the closest hospital to Bangla Road. It has a 24-hour emergency room for first care; serious cases go to the big hospitals in Phuket Town. Phone +66 76 342 633.

items.title: Ambulance and insurance
items.text: Call 1669 for an ambulance (191 also works). Hospitals ask for a payment guarantee or insurance before treatment. Get travel insurance that covers hospital, evacuation and your activities (boats, diving, scooter only with a valid licence). Save the insurer's phone number.

items.title: Pharmacies
items.text: Pharmacies are everywhere, including Boots and Watsons in malls. Many basic medicines are sold without a prescription. Do not buy medicine on the street; it may be fake. Bring your own medicines in the original packs with a copy of the prescription.

items.title: Sun and heat
items.text: In January the midday UV index is high to extreme (about 8-11). Use high-SPF sunscreen, a hat and sunglasses, and stay in the shade around midday. Drink plenty of water, especially at parties. Heat stroke can be deadly.

items.title: Mosquitoes and dengue
items.text: Dengue fever exists in Thailand. The mosquitoes bite mostly in the daytime. Use repellent with 20% or more DEET and sleep in air-con or screened rooms. See a doctor if you get a high fever. Ask your doctor about vaccines such as hepatitis A before the trip.

items.title: Tap water and animals
items.text: Do not drink tap water; drink bottled or filtered water. Keep away from stray dogs and monkeys, as rabies exists. If an animal bites or scratches you, wash the wound with soap and water and see a doctor the same day.

items.title: Dry, hot and sunny
items.text: January is one of the driest months in Phuket. The average high is about 32-33°C and the low about 23-25°C. Rain is about 30-36 mm in the whole month, on about 5-6 days, and a short shower is always possible. Humidity is about 70-76%.

items.title: Sea conditions
items.text: On the west coast (Patong, Karon, Kata, Bang Tao) the Andaman Sea is usually calm and clear in January. The water is about 28°C. It is the best season for swimming, snorkelling and boat trips, but still check the beach flags.

items.title: Sunrise and sunset
items.text: During your trip, sunrise is 06:42-06:46 and sunset 18:23-18:31 (on 19 Jan: 06:45 and 18:28). It gets dark about 20-25 minutes after sunset. West-coast beaches face the sunset.

items.title: Peak season
items.text: January is high season. Prices are highest over Christmas and New Year and stay high all month. Popular tours, boats and good rooms fill up fast, so book the important things early.

items.title: Temples: dress code
items.text: Cover shoulders and knees: no tank tops, short shorts or short skirts. Take off your shoes before you enter a temple building. Do not point your feet at a Buddha image. Some temples lend sarongs at the entrance.

items.title: Royal family: show respect
items.text: Never criticise or joke about the King or the royal family, also not online. It is a crime with long prison terms. Stand when the royal anthem plays, for example in cinemas before the film. Do not step on money, because it shows the King.

items.title: Shoes, head and feet
items.text: Take off your shoes when you enter homes, temples, massage rooms and some shops; if you see shoes at the door, do the same. Do not touch people's heads. Do not point your feet at people or put them on tables.

items.title: The wai
items.text: The wai is the Thai greeting: palms together at the chest and a small bow. Return a wai from adults. You do not need to wai staff or children; a smile and sawasdee krap or ka is fine. Women should not touch monks.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: Tipping is not required but welcome. Many hotels and restaurants add a 10% service charge, so check the bill. Round up taxi fares. Leave about 50-100 baht for a massage or a good guide.

items.title: Haggling
items.text: Bargain at markets, with tuk-tuks and for tours sold on the street. Do not bargain in malls, 7-Eleven, restaurants or shops with fixed prices. Smile and stay calm; anger and shouting do not work in Thailand.

items.title: Plugs and voltage
items.text: Thailand uses 220-230 V, 50 Hz. Most sockets take flat US-style pins (type A/B) and round two-pin European plugs (type C). UK and Australian plugs need an adapter. Phone and laptop chargers marked 100-240 V work fine.

items.title: Grab, Bolt and inDrive
items.text: Install Grab and Bolt before you arrive and add a payment card. Compare both for each ride. inDrive also works in Phuket and lets you offer your own price.

items.title: Google Translate with offline Thai
items.text: Download Thai for offline use in Google Translate. The camera mode reads menus and signs, and conversation mode helps with drivers.

items.title: Google Maps offline area
items.text: Download offline maps of Phuket and Phang Nga (and Koh Phangan if you go). Save your hotel and favourite places. Show the map to drivers to explain where you want to go.

items.title: LINE
items.text: LINE is the main chat app in Thailand. Many hotels, drivers, tour shops and clubs have a LINE account and answer messages there.

items.title: 12Go
items.text: Book ferries, buses, vans and domestic flights in one app. If the trip has an 'e-ticket' sign, the PDF on your phone is enough. If not, print the voucher and swap it for a ticket at the counter. Check the pier and pickup time carefully.

items.title: Klook and GetYourGuide
items.text: Book tours, boat trips and tickets with reviews and clear prices. Check what is included (hotel pickup, park fees, lunch) and the cancellation rules.

items.title: Wise and ATMs
items.text: A Wise or similar card gives a good exchange rate. In 2026 Thai bank ATMs charge foreign cards 250 baht (Visa) or 350 baht (Mastercard) per withdrawal, so take out larger amounts. Always choose to pay in baht (THB), not in your home currency.

items.title: Thailand Tourist Police app
items.text: Official app with an SOS function that connects you to the Tourist Police (1155) and uses GPS to find you. Live chat in English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Russian.

items.title: Be at the airport by 15:20
items.text: For the 18:20 flight, arrive about 3 hours before, by 15:20. Late January is high season, and the lines at check-in, security and passport control can be long. Most airlines close check-in 40-60 minutes before take-off, so check the time on your ticket.

items.title: When to leave for the airport
items.text: Leave Nai Yang by 15:00 (5-10 min), Kamala by 14:15 (40-60 min), Patong by 13:45 (50-90 min) and Kata by 13:15 (60-100 min). Traffic going north gets bad after 16:00, and heavy rain makes it slower.

links.label: Drive times and rush hour (Phuket 101, Mar 2026)

items.title: Book the ride the day before
items.text: In Grab, use 'Advance Booking'. You can book from 90 days to 75 minutes before pickup. The price is fixed and includes a booking fee of about 50-100 baht. Bolt also lets you book up to 90 days ahead. If your hotel books a car, agree the price first.

items.title: Cheapest ride: the Smart Bus
items.text: Smart Bus Route 1 runs along the west coast to the airport for 100 baht. To arrive at about 14:50, take it at Kata Palm 12:47, Patong (Bangla police box) 13:20 or Kamala Big C 13:35. The bus before (12:12, 12:50, 13:05) arrives about 14:20 and is safer with traffic. Timetable from 16 Jan 2026: check it again before you go.

items.title: Check-out is at 11:00 or 12:00
items.text: Most hotels near the airport want you out by 12:00. Proud Phuket's FAQ says 11:00, but its booking terms say 12:00, so ask at check-in. A late check-out depends on free rooms and often costs extra, so ask a few days before. Reception can usually keep your bags for the afternoon.

items.title: Left luggage at the airport
items.text: AIRPORTELs has a counter in the international terminal, on the ground floor (called '1st floor' in Thailand), at Exit 2 (Door 2). It is open 06:00-24:00 and costs 150 baht per bag for 24 hours (Oct 2026). Leave your bags there, then go to Nai Yang Beach, 5-10 minutes away.

items.title: VAT refund: the shopping rules
items.text: Buy in shops with the 'VAT Refund for Tourists' sign and spend at least 2,000 baht (with VAT) in one shop on one day. Show your passport and get the P.P.10 form and the original tax invoice; check that your name and passport number are right. You must fly out within 60 days. Hotels, food and services do not count.

items.title: VAT refund at Phuket airport
items.text: If your goods total 20,000 baht or more, show them with the forms at the Customs VAT counter before check-in. Keep in your hand luggage any watch, phone, laptop, bag or jewellery of 40,000 baht or more, and anything of 100,000 baht or more. After passport control, go to the VAT Refund Office (3rd floor). Up to 30,000 baht is paid in cash there.

items.title: No departure card, and e-gates
items.text: There is no departure card: the paper TM6 card has not been used at airports since July 2022, and the TDAC is only for entering Thailand. Since 13 June 2026, HKT has automatic passport gates for departures. You need an e-passport valid for 6 more months and must be at least 120 cm tall. Take off your hat, glasses and mask.

links.label: TAT: TM6 cancelled for air travel
Thai embassy: TDAC is for entry

items.title: Power banks and liquids
items.text: Power banks go only in hand luggage, max 2 per person. Up to 100 Wh is fine, 100-160 Wh needs airline approval, and bigger or unlabelled ones are not allowed. Since June 2026 you may not use or charge them on the plane; keep them in the seat pocket or under the seat. Liquids: max 100 ml per bottle, in one clear 1-litre bag.

items.title: No departure tax to pay
items.text: The airport passenger fee is already in your ticket price: 1,120 baht for tickets issued from 20 June 2026 (730 baht before). You pay nothing extra at the airport.

items.title: A relaxed last day near the airport
items.text: Check out, then leave your bags at reception or at AIRPORTELs. Have lunch at Natural Restaurant or on Nai Yang Beach, then choose a massage with a free airport drop-off, plane spotting at Mai Khao (best until about 14:00) or the 13:30 tour at Soi Dog (open on Tuesday). Be at the terminal by 15:20.

items.title: Paid lounges after passport control
items.text: The Coral lounges are on the international side, after passport control. You can buy a pass online, for example a 2.5-hour pass for the Coral Executive Lounge on Klook. Priority Pass works only in some of them, so check before you go up.
